steps.what: Read the child's current progress evidence before meeting parents
Meet with parents and guardians to discuss progress, priorities and resource needs
Enter actual parent-discussion priorities in the existing pupil record

tasks.design: Configure a current-goal view and linked meeting-entry fields in the pupil record tool {OTHER}. The teacher reads the evidence, speaks directly with parents and writes the actual priorities for later classroom and support follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress evidence is consulted across views and stable pupil and goal references are retyped into follow-up entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and form fields can remove those repetitions without generating pupil judgements.
tasks.still_hard: Parents may describe needs that the school's evidence has missed.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, build trust and agree realistic priorities with the family.

ambition.what: The teacher retains the same educational responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pupil-linked views and existing follow-up forms can reduce reference copying while progress discussion remains human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual progress review, parent discussion and the existing pupil follow-up entry used by the teacher and authorized support staff. No extra meeting report or parent send is invented.

Teachers produce pupil work observations and current goal references during ordinary teaching; parents supply their account in s2; s3 counts writing the actual outcome. Missing links require original source reading, not a free clean pupil dataset.

s1 removes three units of view navigation. s3 removes three units of repeated pupil and goal references, retaining twelve for actual priorities, factual checks and negligible unchanged same-system save. The save is ungated and earns no saving.
No recording, pupil scoring or automated educational decision is introduced. Shares are illustrative rather than measured.
unknowns: Whether a follow-up entry is actually kept for these meetings
Whether the pupil tool already reuses current goal references
research_questions: Does native linking reduce entry without copying obsolete priorities?

already_counted.description: Read actual evidence, discuss priorities and write the existing follow-up entry

incremental.description: Maintain goal links and repair outdated form references

steps.what: Locate and arrange the selected computer and audio-visual presentation files
Set up and test the computers, audio-visual aids and other equipment
Use the equipment and materials to supplement live presentations

tasks.design: Use lesson-linked folders and saved playback order in {DOCS} and the classroom presentation tool {OTHER}. The teacher still tests the physical setup and chooses when and how to use it during the lesson.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected files require repeated navigation and ordering before the presentation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lesson folders and saved playlists remove that file handling.
tasks.still_hard: A file that plays correctly may still be poorly suited to the class's understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Watch the class and change the explanation or medium when necessary.

ambition.what: Live teaching remains the main work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: lesson-linked file organization can reduce preparation navigation while physical setup and live teaching remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing classroom display, audio and presentation tools. Boundary includes actual file arrangement, physical setup and live use, not creating new teaching content or a lesson report.

The teacher already selected the lesson files during normal planning; s1 still verifies file identity and order. No new content catalogue is assumed. Missing or incompatible files are opened and repaired manually within retained work and upkeep.
Six of twenty file-handling units are repeated searching and ordering; fourteen remain for opening and checking the materials. Existing playback runtime and ordinary file saving earn no saving.
unknowns: Whether lesson files are already grouped
How often presentation files fail to open on classroom equipment
research_questions: Does saved playback order survive the actual classroom setup?

incremental.description: Repair stale lesson links and incompatible playback files

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94 gross6 less upkeep1 gives5. If the lesson uses an unfamiliar file format needing manual arrangement, s1 retains19 of20; physical setup25 and live use55 stay. Gross1 less upkeep1 gives0.

steps.what: Read the individual students' current needs and progress evidence
Meet with other professionals to discuss students' needs and progress
Update the existing classroom support entry with actual discussion implications

tasks.design: Configure links to current support goals in the pupil record tool {OTHER} and prefill stable references in the existing classroom support entry. Professionals discuss the individual child directly, and the teacher records only the actual classroom implications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current support references are spread across record sections and copied again into working entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native goal links and reference fields can remove that clerical repetition.
tasks.still_hard: Different professionals can reasonably interpret incomplete evidence differently.
tasks.human_edge: Bring classroom knowledge to the discussion and translate advice into workable support.

ambition.what: Professional judgement and responsibilities remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked pupil support fields can reduce navigation and reference entry while professional discussion remains human.

assumptions: Boundary includes the teacher's real preparation, participation and working classroom support entry used during teaching. No separate meeting minutes or external send is invented.

Authorized professionals and teachers maintain the existing support goals and observations. The teacher supplies the actual discussion implications in s3; missing source context is read manually. OTHER means the restricted pupil record tool.

s1 removes three units of navigation, retaining twelve for evidence reading. s3 removes1.5 units of stable goal references, retaining13.5 for substantive support wording and checks. The ordinary save is negligible, unchanged and ungated.
No recording, diagnosis or automatic pupil judgement is introduced.
unknowns: Whether the teacher maintains a real working support entry
Which professional records the teacher is authorized to access
research_questions: Do links expose current support context without widening access?

incremental.description: Maintain restricted support references and repair stale links

tasks.short: Set and explain clear learning objectives

steps.what: Read curriculum requirements and prior lesson evidence for the objectives
Establish the appropriate lesson, unit and project objectives
Write clear student-facing wording for the selected objectives

loop.purpose: Draft age-appropriate wording for teacher-selected objectives
loop.input: Selected objectives and fixed curriculum goal wording without pupil identifiers
loop.check: Teacher verifies that every objective preserves the intended skill, challenge and evidence of success, not merely the goal code
loop.stop: Changed meaning or unclear success criteria require manual wording; one redraft maximum
loop.why_not_simpler: Plain-language wording varies with the lesson while the educational choice stays human

steps.what: Check the final objectives for clear and achievable classroom meaning
Communicate the objectives to students and clarify what success means

tasks.design: Use existing curriculum templates in {DOCS} before adding a bounded rewrite of objectives the teacher has already chosen. The teacher checks their educational meaning and explains them directly to students; no model selects the child's level or evaluates attainment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clear student-facing objective wording is repeatedly written from formal curriculum language.
tasks.enabler_now: A small source-bound rewrite can propose wording without making the educational decision.
tasks.still_hard: An objective must be appropriate, meaningful and genuinely achievable in the actual lesson.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the right learning challenge and notice when students misunderstand it.

ambition.what: Offer a concrete success example beside a checked objective when the lesson supports one.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a bounded rewrite can help express teacher-selected objectives, but educational selection and semantic verification remain human.

assumptions: Boundary covers objective selection, real written wording and live explanation. The written objective is used in the lesson; no extra pupil progress record or electronic publication is invented.

Curriculum staff produce goal code and wording; the teacher reads existing lesson evidence in s1 and selects the actual objectives in s2. The drafting input contains those selected goals, not a new pupil-data feed.
Native templates are tested first. s3 retains12.5 of25 wording units for checking and repair, plus the separate full final meaning check in s4. Save in DOCS is negligible, unchanged and ungated.
The estimate concerns wording help only, without automatic educational assessment or level setting. Extra draft repair is funded below.
unknowns: How often an existing objective template already fits
Whether generated wording changes the intended learning challenge
research_questions: Can teachers verify preserved meaning and success criteria as quickly as expected?

already_counted.description: Read evidence, select objectives, review draft meaning, check final wording and explain it

incremental.description: Maintain goal templates and repair difficult wording cases

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R87.5 gross12.5 less upkeep3 gives9.5. For a novel project needing almost bespoke wording, s3 retains21 of25 while source20, selection30, final check15 and explanation10 remain. R96 gross4 less upkeep3 gives1.
